title: Welsh FA chief calls for Infantino to step down
dek: Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney has called for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to step down, citing damage to football from his attempted privatization of World Cup rights. Wales is now the first home nation to withdraw backing for Infantino's re-election bid.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: FAW chief Noel Mooney called for Infantino's resignation after the FIFA president's plan to sell 21% of competition rights to private investors sparked confederation backlash.
bottom_line: Infantino faces mounting pressure from multiple confederations ahead of his re-election bid. Watch for other home nations or confederations to withdraw support and for the timing of the re-election vote, which will determine whether this pressure translates into a contested race.
body: Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney called for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to step down, according to BBC Sport. Mooney cited damage to football caused by Infantino's attempted World Cup privatization plan as the reason for his call.

Infantino has faced heavy criticism for proposing a structure that would have created a new company to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all FIFA competitions, including World Cups, with 21% of stakes to be sold to a private investment company, per BBC Sport. That sell-off plan has been scrapped.

Wales became the first home nation to withdraw backing for Infantino's re-election bid earlier this month, according to BBC Sport. Scotland has also withdrawn support in a parallel move that signals fracturing confederal backing for the FIFA president, who has held office since 2016.

Mooney, who previously worked alongside Infantino at UEFA, acknowledged that Infantino did very good work as general secretary of that organization. Mooney cited Arsene Wenger's technical development scheme as an example of forward progress under Infantino's tenure, according to BBC Sport, tempering his criticism with recognition of prior accomplishments.
